author: Bloomberg
description:
Flavio Bolsonaro said he would work with the US and China if he becomes Brazil’s president, after a surprise election performance left him poised to join a wave of conservative leaders pushing Latin America closer to Washington.
“I’m not going to pick sides,” Bolsonaro said at an event in Brasilia on Thursday. “My side will be the Brazilian people, whether we’re dealing with China, Israel, the Middle East, Argentina or India. It doesn’t matter. That’s how I’m going to govern.”
Bolsonaro finished...
title: Flavio Bolsonaro says he would work with China and US as Brazil’s president

author: Victoria Bela
description:
Chinese researchers have developed a catalyst that converts synthesis gas into sustainable jet fuel – a breakthrough that could boost production, help meet net-zero carbon goals and yield a gross profit margin exceeding 50 per cent.
The team verified the efficacy of the chemical catalyst in a thousand-tonne pilot test and found that combining woody biomass-derived synthesis gas, or syngas, with the cobalt-manganese catalyst enabled the “highly efficient synthesis of jet fuel”.
Based on a...
title: China breakthrough projected to push sustainable jet fuel gross profit margin past 50%

author: Teresa Elena Frontado
description:
The United States has downgraded Hong Kong to the lowest tier in its annual human trafficking report, citing shortcomings in prosecutions and victim identification, an assessment the city’s government rejected as “entirely unfounded”.
The US State Department’s 2026 Trafficking in Persons (TIP) Report, released on Thursday, moved Hong Kong from the Tier 2 Watch List, where it had been listed for two consecutive years, to Tier 3.
That places the city alongside mainland China and Macau among 20...
title: Hong Kong rejects US downgrade to lowest tier in human trafficking report

author: Seong Hyeon Choi
description:
The Pentagon announced on Thursday a new multimillion-dollar initiative for “maintaining American leadership” in quantum computing capabilities amid accelerating competition between the US and China over the military application of advanced technology.
In a press release, the Office of the Under Secretary of Defence for Research and Engineering, which serves as the US Department of Defence’s chief technology adviser, announced that the new initiative, worth around $350 million, is aimed at...
title: Pentagon unveils US$350 million quantum computing push as China rivalry grows

author: Han Li
description:
The Trump administration is launching an investigation into nine US universities over alleged J-1 visa fraud, with officials raising concerns about Chinese scholars and the Chinese government.
The J-1 programme covers exchange visitors including international researchers, scholars and students, who may receive temporary authorisation to work or conduct research in the US.
At a Thursday press conference, Anthony D’Esposito, inspector general of the US Department of Labor, announced what he called...
title: US investigates 9 universities over alleged visa fraud, with focus on China

author: Igor Patrick
description:
BYD is studying whether to manufacture lithium batteries in Argentina, Foreign Minister Pablo Quirno said on Thursday after meeting Stella Li, the Chinese electric vehicle maker’s executive vice-president.
According to Quirno, the company was looking at “investment opportunities in Argentina linked to the lithium value chain, particularly in the production of batteries and energy storage systems”. He did not say how much BYD might spend or where the factory could go.
The minister tied the talks...
title: China’s BYD considering lithium battery plant in Argentina, foreign minister says

author: Seong Hyeon Choi
description:
Washington’s policy towards Taiwan is increasingly tied to its relationship with Beijing, according to former US officials who also warn that the war in Iran is weakening US military readiness for a potential conflict in the Taiwan Strait.
During a fireside chat in an annual symposium hosted by the Global Taiwan Institute in Washington on Wednesday, Brent Christensen, former director of the Taipei Office of the American Institute in Taiwan (AIT), said Washington’s policy towards the self-ruled...
title: Washington’s transactional Taiwan policy puts Indo-Pacific at risk, ex-US officials warn

author: Liu Zhen
description:
The Chinese navy says it had a rare South China Sea encounter involving a foreign warship that lost power, propulsion and radar while following a People’s Liberation Army destroyer, an account that resembles incidents this year involving US Navy destroyers in the region.
The incident occurred when a foreign vessel conducted aggressive close shadowing of the PLA Navy Type 055 destroyer Zunyi during routine training by the Chinese vessel, state broadcaster CCTV reported on Wednesday.
The CCTV...
title: Did a US warship lose power while chasing a Chinese destroyer in the South China Sea?

author: Asad Ullah
description:
Two summits in five months between US President Donald Trump and President Xi Jinping have produced shared language but not an open Strait of Hormuz. After the May meeting in Beijing, there was little sign the two sides agreed on how to end the war. Xi’s visit to Washington yielded no breakthrough on Iran, though Xi backed a return to the interim US-Iran agreement.
Last week, Trump rejected a truce proposal from Iran and said he was considering resuming US bombing of Iran after the midterm...
title: It’s time for China to offer more than statements on Hormuz

author: Gabriel Dominguez
description:
Japan and the United States will rehearse moving anti-ship missiles, air defences and communications networks onto islands near Taiwan this month in an expanded military exercise that analysts say could complicate Beijing’s planning for a Taiwan or East China Sea conflict.
Keen Sword 27, which runs from October 19 to 29, will involve about 45,000 Japanese personnel, 6,100 vehicles, 40 ships and 260 aircraft, up from about 33,000 personnel, 30 ships and 250 aircraft in 2024.
About 12,000 US...
title: How expanded Japan-US military exercises could complicate PLA planning over Taiwan

author: Cao Jiaxuan
description:
China has nominated health official Song Li to run for director general of the World Health Organization, the foreign ministry confirmed on Thursday.
If elected, Song would be the first person from mainland China to head the United Nations health agency.
China previously backed Margaret Chan, a Hong Kong-born doctor and former director of health of Hong Kong, who served as WHO director general from 2007 to 2017.
Song’s nomination comes as the WHO faces a major funding shake-up following the US...
title: China nominates Song Li for WHO chief as agency faces funding shake-up from US exit

author: Carol Yang
description:
An aide to Russia’s president arrived in China on Thursday for a visit that will be closely watched for signs of preparation for a possible trilateral summit with the US during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation leaders’ meeting next month.
Nikolai Patrushev, who is also chairman of Russia’s Maritime Board, was set to hold talks with Foreign Minister Wang Yi, China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced on Wednesday.
Leading a delegation that included representatives from government...
title: Kremlin aide visits China amid speculation about potential Xi-Putin-Trump meeting

author: Neil Denslow,Raymond Ma
description:
US President Donald Trump pressed Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping during last month’s summit to end a deep freeze in relations with Japan’s Sanae Takaichi, the South China Morning Post reported.
Trump raised Japan’s grievances over Chinese restrictions imposed following Takaichi’s comment in November that the Japanese military might intervene in the event of conflict in the Taiwan Strait, according to Thursday’s report, which cited people familiar with the discussions. Beijing regards Taiwan as...
title: Trump pushed Xi to end Japan freeze, but Chinese leader unmoved

author: Victoria Bela
description:
Chinese scientists have created a wearable all-in-one device combining a glucose sensor and insulin micropump that they say paves the way for a fully autonomous mini artificial pancreas, although it has so far only been tested on mice.
Unlike existing commercial systems for managing diabetes that typically require patients to wear two separate patches for monitoring and hormone delivery, the new prototype combines both functions in a single coin-sized device.
Researchers from the University of...
title: Chinese team says its all-in-one mini artificial pancreas offers next-gen diabetes care

author: Junjie Wang
title: Xi-Trump summit outcomes

author: Khushboo Razdan
description:
A federal judge on Wednesday ordered Wanying “Heather” Zhang be held in custody, after her lawyers – who had fought to keep her out of jail – said she “looks forward to establishing” her innocence at trial.
They argued that the US government’s case centred on a single day of alleged surveillance in Seattle and was not evidence that she posed a flight risk.
US Magistrate Judge Steve Kim sided with prosecutors, who told him that Zhang’s parents and siblings lived in China and that her brother had...
title: US judge blocks release of alleged Beijing agent accused of filming Taiwan leader’s son

author: Finbarr Bermingham,Dewey Sim
description:
German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier is planning to visit China in the coming weeks, even as relations between the two countries sour over trade, according to multiple sources familiar with the arrangement.
It will mark the first official visit to China since 2018 for Steinmeier, a former foreign minister whose decade-long tenure as president ends in March 2027. The visit will coincide with Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s trips to Japan and South Korea before the end of October.
Germany’s...
title: German President Steinmeier targets China trip as Berlin sharpens trade stance

author: Cao Jiaxuan
description:
The US has ended its military mission in Iraq, a move analysts said could give Baghdad more room for diversified partnerships and indirectly benefit China’s energy and commercial interests.
But they cautioned that the shift was unlikely to create a power vacuum for Beijing to fill, with China lacking both the ambition and capacity to take on the US security role.
The United States formally ended its Operation Inherent Resolve mission in Iraq on September 30, completing a withdrawal agreed on in...
title: US wraps up military mission in Iraq, giving Baghdad room to strengthen China ties

author: Khushboo Razdan,Fan Chen
description:
Washington and Beijing may have signed an agreement built around “reciprocity”. But a more consequential question remains unresolved: does it mean equal status for Beijing? Countries without a seat at the table are watching that ambiguity closely.
The spectacle of Chinese President Xi Jinping’s state visit to Washington – the tarmac greeting, the flyovers, the state dinner – has been interpreted less as courtesy than as a statement of rank. Some argue that China is no longer being treated as...
title: The ‘G2’ illusion? After Xi-Trump summit, China wants equality while the US seeks deals

author: Chow Chung-yan
description:
This year’s Chinese National Day reception in Washington felt noticeably jollier than those I have attended in recent years. The mood was more relaxed and Chinese Ambassador Xie Feng’s opening speech was upbeat. He even joked about the panda ambassadors at his own expense.
The cheerful tone followed President Xi Jinping’s short but successful state visit to the US, during which his counterpart, President Donald Trump, gave him an unprecedented high-level reception that would have flattered even...
title: Beyond the summit: how US-China relations could still unravel

author: Nayan Seth,Zhang Tong
description:
The United States should engage with Chinese carmakers and battery manufacturers “strategically”, using targeted safeguards instead of the current “wholesale restrictions”, which could lead US carmakers to lose global market share, according to experts.
“We need to consider strategic partnerships,” said John Helveston, an associate professor at George Washington University, during a discussion on Tuesday.
“So not just wholesale restrictions, but look at some of the best opportunities and let...
title: End ‘wholesale restrictions’ on Chinese EVs in US, experts say
